newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks plunge, Nikkei down over 800 points.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks plunge, Nikkei down over 800 points.

text.p: Tokyo stocks plummeted on Friday, with the market benchmark index falling more than 800 points or four percent on worries about the economy and the troubled banking sector.
With less than an hour left in trading for the week, the benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading companies was hit by waves of sell offers.
As the slide continued, it tumbled at one stage by more than 900 points to 17,123.58, a loss of over five percent. This came on top of a drop of more than 600 points on Thursday.
Technical analysts said the market could hope to find some support as it approached the 17,000 level, but if it passed through that barrier it could approach the low of 14,000 last seen in 1992.

Analysts say the market is being pushed lower by gloom about the state of the Japanese economy and worries about higher taxes. The sensitive banking sector is being hardest hit due to massive problem loans left over from the collapse of real estate values, which had soared in the 1980s.
